title: Mi día
goal: Say what you do on a normal day with regular -ar verbs, name the days of the week and say at what time.

lessons.title: Hablar: the -ar pattern
lessons.notes:
Most Spanish verbs end in **-ar**, and almost all of them follow one pattern. Take off -ar and add an ending for the person:
**yo** habl**o** · **tú** habl**as** · **él / ella / usted** habl**a** · **nosotros** habl**amos** · **ellos / ustedes** habl**an**
(Spain: vosotros habl**áis**.)
Learn this once and you can use hundreds of verbs: **trabajar → trabajo, trabajas...**, **estudiar → estudio, estudias...**
The ending already says who, so **Hablo inglés** needs no 'yo'. The present also covers 'I'm speaking' and 'I do speak'.

items.note: Also a noun: el trabajo = work, the job.

sentences.es: Hablo inglés y un poco de español.
sentences.en: I speak English and a little Spanish.
accept_en: I speak English and a bit of Spanish.

lessons.title: More everyday verbs
lessons.notes:
Every verb here works exactly like hablar - no new endings to learn, just new stems:
**escuchar** → escucho, escuchas, escucha, escuchamos, escuchan
**Tomar** is to take, and also to have a drink: **Tomo un café.** (Spain uses tomar too, and **coger** for taking a bus - avoid coger in much of Latin America, where it's vulgar.)
**Mirar** is to look at / watch: **Miramos la televisión.**
To say 'not', **no** goes right before the verb: **No cocino.**
**Mucho** (a lot) after a verb: **Trabajo mucho.** **Tarde** = late; **en casa** = at home.

sentences.en: I listen to music in the car.
accept_en: I'm listening to music in the car.

sentences.es: Miramos la televisión en la sala.
sentences.en: We watch TV in the living room.
accept_en: We watch television in the lounge room.
We're watching TV in the living room.
I drink a coffee with milk.
I have a coffee with milk.
My mom is a very good cook.

sentences.en: We don't listen to the music.
accept_en: We aren't listening to the music.

lessons.title: Days of the week
lessons.notes:
The days have no capital letter and are all masculine: **el lunes, el martes, el miércoles, el jueves, el viernes, el sábado, el domingo**. The Spanish week starts on Monday.
The article does the job of 'on': **el lunes** = on Monday; **los lunes** = on Mondays (every Monday). No word for 'on'!
Days ending in -s don't change in the plural: el lunes → los lunes; sábado and domingo add -s.
**Mañana** means tomorrow (and also morning - unit 11). **De lunes a viernes** = Monday to Friday.

accept_en: I work from Monday to Friday.

sentences.es: Los sábados camino en la playa.
sentences.en: On Saturdays I walk on the beach.
accept_en: I walk on the beach on Saturdays.

sentences.es: El domingo cocino para mi familia.
sentences.en: On Sunday I cook for my family.
accept_en: I'm cooking for my family on Sunday.

sentences.es: Estudio español los martes y los jueves.
sentences.en: I study Spanish on Tuesdays and Thursdays.
accept_en: I study Spanish on Tuesday and Thursday.

sentences.es: El fin de semana miro la televisión.
sentences.en: At the weekend I watch TV.
accept_en: On the weekend I watch television.
I watch TV at the weekend.

lessons.title: At what time?
lessons.notes:
**¿A qué hora...?** asks at what time something happens. Answer with **a la una** (at one) or **a las** + number for the rest - 'las horas' is feminine plural: **a las dos, a las ocho**.
Add **y media** for half past and **en punto** for 'on the dot': **a las seis y media**, **a las nueve en punto**. (Unit 11 does telling the time in full.)
How often: **siempre** (always), **normalmente** (normally), **a veces** (sometimes), **nunca** (never), **todos los días** (every day). They usually go before the verb: **Nunca cocino.** **Temprano** = early.

accept_en: At what time do you arrive?
What time do you get there?

sentences.es: Siempre tomo un café a las siete.
sentences.en: I always have a coffee at seven.
accept_en: I always drink a coffee at seven.

sentences.es: La clase es a la una.
accept_en: The class is at one o'clock.

sentences.es: Llegamos a las nueve en punto.
sentences.en: We arrive at nine o'clock sharp.
accept_en: We arrive at nine on the dot.
We get there at nine sharp.

sentences.es: La clase es a las seis y media.
sentences.en: The class is at half past six.
accept_en: The class is at six thirty.
The lesson is at half past six.
